config.title: Lazy Loading Routes

intro.title: Lazy Loading Routes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application with multiple feature modules that load only when needed. You'll learn the core concept of lazy loading, which improves your app's performance by splitting code into smaller bundles. The main technologies involved are Angular's RouterModule, loadChildren syntax, and feature modules. By the end, you'll understand how to configure routes to load modules on-demand, making your app faster and more efficient.
intro.usecase: Lazy loading routes is essential for large-scale Angular applications like e-commerce platforms and enterprise dashboards. When users navigate between sections like product catalogs, admin panels, or analytics modules, lazy loading ensures only the necessary code loads, dramatically improving initial load times. This pattern is particularly valuable in applications with complex feature sets where users may never visit certain sections during a session. Developers implement this to optimize performance while maintaining clean, modular code architecture that scales with business needs.

objectives: Configure lazy-loaded routes in the Angular router module
Construct feature modules with separate routing configurations
Implement route definitions that reference lazy-loaded modules
Apply the loadChildren property to defer module loading
Initialize application structure with multiple lazy-loaded feature areas
Integrate lazy loading into an existing Angular application
Manipulate route configurations to optimize initial bundle size

steps.title: Import RouterModule and Routes from @angular/router
steps.instruction: In your main app module file, import RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the same module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Angular core modules
import { Component, NgModule } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The RouterModule and Routes symbols are imported and available for use in your app module.
successCriteria: RouterModule and Routes are imported from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both RouterModule and Routes from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please import both RouterModule and Routes from the '@angular/router' package.

steps.title: Create a new feature module with routing
steps.instruction: Generate a new feature module named 'LazyFeatureModule' with routing using Angular CLI or manually create it.
steps.hint: You can use the Angular CLI command 'ng generate module lazy-feature --routing' or manually create a module file with routing configuration.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new feature module named 'LazyFeatureModule' is created with routing capabilities.
successCriteria: The 'LazyFeatureModule' is defined with @NgModule decorator and includes RouterModule.forChild() in its imports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a module, but make sure it includes routing configuration (RouterModule.forChild()).
steps.feedbackWrong: The module wasn't created correctly. Ensure you define a class with @NgModule decorator and include routing.

steps.title: Define routes in the feature module
steps.instruction: Inside the feature module's routing configuration, define a routes array with at least one route object. Use the Routes type you imported earlier.
steps.hint: The routes array should be typed as Routes and contain route objects with path and component properties.
steps.seedCode:
import { RouterModule, Routes } from '@angular/router';

// Define your routes array here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a properly typed routes array defined in your feature module's routing configuration.
successCriteria: A routes array of type Routes is defined with at least one route object containing path and component properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your routes array is properly typed as Routes and contains at least one complete route object with both path and component properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The routes array definition is missing or incomplete. Remember to create a routes array with the Routes type and include route objects with path and component properties.

steps.title: Configure lazy loading route in main app routing
steps.instruction: In the main AppRoutingModule (or your main routing file), add a route object with a path property set to 'feature' and a loadChildren property that uses the import() syntax to load the feature module.
steps.hint: Use the loadChildren property with a function that returns import('./path/to/feature.module').then(m => m.FeatureModule).
steps.expectedOutcome: A routes array with one route object that has path and loadChildren properties configured for lazy loading.
successCriteria: The routes array contains a route object with path: 'feature' and loadChildren using import() syntax pointing to the feature module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your route object has both the path and loadChildren properties. The loadChildren should use the import() syntax with the correct module path.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route configuration isn't quite right. Remember to create a route object with path and loadChildren properties. The loadChildren should use dynamic import syntax to load the feature module.

steps.title: Remove feature module from main app module imports
steps.instruction: Open the main AppModule file (typically app.module.ts) and remove the import statement and reference to the feature module from the imports array.
steps.hint: Look for the feature module (e.g., FeatureModule) in the imports array of @NgModule decorator in app.module.ts and delete that line.
steps.expectedOutcome: The feature module is no longer eagerly loaded in the main AppModule, ensuring it will be lazy-loaded via the route configuration.
successCriteria: The feature module is removed from the imports array in AppModule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but ensure the feature module is completely removed from the imports array in AppModule. Double-check the file.
steps.feedbackWrong: The feature module still appears in the AppModule imports. Remove it to enable lazy loading.

steps.title: Add router-outlet to main app component template
steps.instruction: In your main app component template (app.component.html), add the <router-outlet></router-outlet> element to serve as the placeholder where lazy-loaded content will be rendered.
steps.hint: The router-outlet directive acts as a container that Angular Router uses to display the component associated with the current route.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: adding a router outlet in a template -->
<router-outlet></router-outlet>
steps.expectedOutcome: The main app component template now contains a router-outlet element that will display the components loaded via lazy loading.
successCriteria: The app.component.html file contains a <router-outlet></router-outlet> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the complete <router-outlet></router-outlet> element in your app.component.html file.
steps.feedbackWrong: The router-outlet element is missing. Add <router-outlet></router-outlet> to your main app component template to create the placeholder for lazy-loaded content.

steps.title: Add preloading strategy import
steps.instruction: Import PreloadAllModules from '@angular/router' in your routing file.
steps.hint: Add the import statement at the top of your file, alongside the existing RouterModule and Routes imports.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a module for preloading
import { PreloadAllModules } from '@angular/router';
steps.expectedOutcome: The PreloadAllModules strategy is imported and available for use in route configuration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing PreloadAllModules from '@angular/router'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import is missing or incorrect. You need to import PreloadAllModules from '@angular/router'.

steps.title: Configure preloading strategy in main routing
steps.instruction: In the RouterModule.forRoot() configuration in your main routing module, add the preloadingStrategy property set to PreloadAllModules.
steps.hint: Add the preloadingStrategy property to the configuration object passed to RouterModule.forRoot().
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Adding preloading strategy to router configuration
RouterModule.forRoot(routes, { preloadingStrategy: PreloadAllModules })
steps.expectedOutcome: The router configuration now includes preloading strategy to improve user experience by loading lazy modules in the background.
successCriteria: RouterModule.forRoot() includes the preloadingStrategy property set to PreloadAllModules.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the preloadingStrategy property to the RouterModule.forRoot() configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: The preloading strategy wasn't configured correctly. Check that you added the preloadingStrategy property to RouterModule.forRoot().

steps.title: Verify preloading behavior
steps.instruction: Run the application using `ng serve` and open the browser's Developer Tools to monitor network requests for preloaded chunks.
steps.hint: In the Network tab, look for requests to JavaScript chunk files (like feature-module.js) that load after the initial page load, indicating preloading is working.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see JavaScript chunk files being loaded after the initial page load in the Network tab, confirming preloading is active.
successCriteria: Network tab shows chunk files loading after initial page load, confirming preloading strategy is working.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're looking in the Network tab of Developer Tools and reloading the page to see the chunk file requests.
steps.feedbackWrong: Run `ng serve`, open Developer Tools (F12), go to the Network tab, reload the page, and look for JavaScript chunk files loading after the initial page.

steps.title: Test navigation between lazy loaded modules
steps.instruction: Navigate between the routes in your browser and verify that the lazy-loaded chunks load correctly when you click the navigation links.
steps.hint: Open your application in the browser, click the navigation links you created earlier, and check the browser's Network tab to see the JavaScript chunks being loaded.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should be able to navigate between routes and see the lazy-loaded modules loading as separate JavaScript chunks in the browser's Network tab.
successCriteria: Navigation works between routes and lazy-loaded chunks load on demand
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Navigation works but you might not have verified chunk loading. Check the Network tab in browser dev tools to see the JavaScript files loading when you navigate.
steps.feedbackWrong: Navigation isn't working as expected. Make sure your routes are properly configured and the navigation links use the correct routerLink paths.
